what_happened: render_next()'s existing terminal-member-omission convention and build_ready_pool()'s readiness predicate together gave an exact, reusable precedent for the roadmap-aware candidate filter -- no new readiness logic had to be designed, and a live jq simulation against the current state.json confirmed the proposed walk-and-filter rule behaves sensibly (4 leading batches skip at zero probe cost, 5th batch's singleton [577] is the first live candidate).

Research report 01 pre-settled the design decision (Direction (a)) with live-corpus validation and an enumerated test list, so plan authoring needed only sizing/sequencing plus two new mechanical findings (usage() sed-range coupling at orchestrate-suggest-next-batch.sh:99 and the index-entries.json line_count coupling for the template edit); no re-derivation of the diagnosis was needed.

Plan phases 1-4 edit the source store (agent-system/extensions/core/**) with redeploy deferred to Phase 5, but this suite's default CORE_TEST_SUBJECT_MODE resolution is deploy-tree-first: it silently resolves and copies the STALE deployed .claude/scripts/orchestrate-suggest-next-batch.sh into build_scratch() rather than the edited source-store copy, unless CORE_TEST_SUBJECT_MODE=source-store is exported. Phase 1 and Phase 2's own run-all.sh --only invocations (run without that override) therefore validated the pre-edit deployed script, not the edits -- a false-confidence result that happened not to produce a false PASS only because the pre-existing cases are genuinely unchanged by the refactor. Re-ran both phases' verification with CORE_TEST_SUBJECT_MODE=source-store exported and confirmed all cases, including the new Phase 3 roadmap-walk cases, pass against the actual edited script.

Phase 3's Scope Hypothesis declared the test file alone, but writing the new roadmap-walk regression cases surfaced a real bug in Phase 2's own implementation: mode_next_batch() populated READY_SET by calling build_ready_set() (via build_ready_pool()) inside a process-substitution subshell (done < <(build_ready_pool)), so the associative array never persisted back to the parent shell where task_is_ready() is later called from suggest_from_roadmap_batches() -- every batch was therefore seen as empty-filtered regardless of real readiness. Fixed by calling build_ready_set() directly in mode_next_batch()'s own shell before building the ready array. Also added a visible 'Authored roadmap batch N: skipped' line for an empty-filtered batch (Phase 2's own text only recorded the skip in a counter, not visibly, which could not satisfy the new case (o) acceptance -- 'first batch's skip is visible in the output'). Both fixes landed in orchestrate-suggest-next-batch.sh during Phase 3, a declared excursion beyond that phase's test-file-only Scope Hypothesis, recorded here rather than silently absorbed.
